2.content:
This Statement of Work covers Bristlecone’s implementation services for Google Silicon COT Supply Chain, using a global-template approach to standardize core processes while accommodating approved localization needs and required system dependencies across the deployment landscape.

- Establish and sign off a global design template through structured planning, design workshops, baseline configuration, and stakeholder review.
- Deliver the implementation through phased execution including integration and data activities, sprint-based build, testing, training, and hypercare support.
- Enable adoption and governance through project management, organizational change management, risk control, and defined stakeholder participation across onsite and offshore delivery.

Deferred decisions, assumptions, and any open scope items are captured in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

3.1.content:
Google is establishing a standardized Silicon COT Supply Chain model that spans foundry and OSAT operations, core procurement and subcontracting flows, batch and lot traceability, enterprise structure, and planning-system dependencies. The current landscape requires a clear AS-IS baseline across front-end and back-end processes, including material master setup, subcontracting settlement, genealogy, cost-model integration, and existing collaboration through E2Open.

Key pain points include variation between global and regional requirements, gaps in current organizational and master-data structures for the Silicon business, incomplete alignment of lot-level and unit-level system boundaries, and dependency on external integrations such as MES, PLM, E2Open, and Kinaxis. This engagement is driven by the need to define a global design template, harmonize core processes and data, validate technical mappings, and create an execution-ready plan that supports controlled localization and coordinated deployment across the in-scope landscape.

3.2.content:
- Establish an agreed AS-IS baseline for Silicon COT supply chain processes, data, and system interactions.
- Define a global To-Be design template for procurement, subcontracting, traceability, and related supply chain operations.
- Harmonize organizational structure, master data, and core process design across in-scope entities and sites.
- Confirm end-to-end data flows and integration requirements across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and other dependent systems.
- Validate design assumptions, scope boundaries, and stakeholder requirements through structured workshops and playback sessions.
- Develop a sprint-based execution plan with defined scope, priorities, dependencies, governance, and ownership.
- Support deployment readiness through a standardized approach that accommodates approved local variations.

3.3.content:
The target state is a standardized Silicon COT Supply Chain process anchored on a global design template and executed through coordinated regional deployment. Demand, supply, and planning signals flow through the approved planning and collaboration landscape, with defined interfaces into SAP S/4HANA for transactional execution. Procurement and subcontracting processes support foundry and OSAT operations, while material, batch, and genealogy data are structured to enable traceability from wafer lot through probe, die bank, assembly, test, and finished goods. The design incorporates harmonized enterprise structure, controlled localization, and governed integration dependencies across MES, PLM, E2Open, Kinaxis, and other approved systems.

<IMAGE id="689305094e2e"/>

The indicative process flow is:
- Plan and collaborate across approved planning and partner platforms.
- Convert requirements into purchase and subcontracting transactions in SAP S/4HANA.
- Execute foundry, OSAT, goods movement, and yield-related processes with defined traceability controls.
- Ingest and reconcile operational, batch, and partner data across system boundaries.
- Produce cost, yield, and genealogy reporting to support execution and decision-making.

4.1.content: The engagement covers Google’s Silicon supply chain operations for the in-scope partner and execution footprint in Taiwan and North America. In-scope locations include TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL in Taiwan, together with the Google Hub and warehouse operations required to support the approved process and system design. Delivery will be performed through a combined onsite and offshore model, with onsite support aligned to North America and offshore delivery supporting build, integration, and related workstreams. Any expansion to additional countries, plants, warehouses, business units, or partner sites requires review through the agreed change management process.

4.2.content: In scope are the end-to-end Silicon Customer Owned Tooling supply chain processes needed to establish standardized planning, procurement, subcontracting, and traceability operations across the approved landscape. This includes constrained supply planning with yield considerations, material master design and governance, batch and lot traceability, foundry and OSAT process alignment, procurement execution, subcontracting flows, inventory-related planning, and the supporting process interactions needed to improve the ASIC commit process. The scope also includes AS-IS discovery, fit-gap assessment, To-Be process design, and validation of process handoffs across planning, execution, collaboration, and reporting systems.

4.3.content: Technical scope includes the implementation and configuration activities required across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and approved dependent platforms supporting the Silicon COT process. In scope are SAP S/4HANA Production Planning and Materials Management process enablement, Kinaxis setup for supply, constraint, and inventory planning, delta integration development using BTP-IS, and adaptation of existing data templates to support Silicon planning needs. Existing integration frameworks are expected to be leveraged where available, including Google’s current framework used for machines planning, with incremental delta interfaces included in scope subject to discovery confirmation. Also in scope are resource master, yield, unit-of-measure, capacity, CM-data, and related interface analysis and implementation required for the approved process design.

4.4.content: Services in scope include project management, fit-gap analysis, AS-IS and To-Be process design, business process design documentation, functional specifications for approved custom development, configuration and build, test planning and execution, unit testing, system integration testing, UAT support, regression testing, performance testing, data migration support, cutover planning and execution, hypercare, organizational change management, train-the-trainer support, and knowledge transfer to the support team. Delivery will follow a phased agile model across Explore, Build, and Deploy. Cross-functional consulting leadership will coordinate the SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and integration workstreams across onsite and offshore resources.

4.5.content: Application scope includes Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, and E2Open, together with the approved connected landscape needed to support the Silicon COT process. Within Kinaxis, the in-scope capabilities are Supply Planning, Constraint Planning, Inventory Planning, Analytics and Reporting, and Data Integration. Within SAP S/4HANA, the in-scope capabilities are Production Planning, Materials Management, and process integration required for the approved solution. Controlling support is expected to be staffed by Google. Application interactions with PLM, BigQuery, MES, Test Hub, and related systems are in scope to the extent required for approved interface design, data exchange, traceability boundaries, and reporting enablement.

5.content:
The solution architecture uses Kinaxis as the planning orchestration layer, SAP S/4HANA as the transactional execution backbone, and E2Open as the supplier-collaboration channel for foundry and OSAT interactions. The architecture supports closed-loop planning and execution across demand, supply, procurement, subcontracting, inventory, traceability, and reporting processes required for the Silicon COT model.

Integration is designed around master and transactional data flows between SAP S/4HANA and Kinaxis, supplier-collaboration exchanges through E2Open, and approved downstream analytics and engineering data dependencies. The target design retains Google’s existing integration framework where feasible and extends it with approved delta interfaces to support Silicon-specific data ingestion, validation, and handoff requirements. Boundary control will be maintained between lot-level process and collaboration data and unit-level test or analytics processing.

Deployment will follow a phased, wave-based implementation model across Explore, Build, and Deploy, with SAP S/4HANA and Kinaxis delivered as coordinated workstreams and E2Open support included where required for approved interface enablement. The architecture is intended to scale for subsequent rollout waves, additional approved planning scenarios, and future analytics use cases without changing the core execution and collaboration pattern.

Change governance will be managed through a program structure that wraps the delivery with project management, integration governance, and process and change-management controls. Design decisions will be baselined before configuration, and changes affecting scope, timelines, integrations, data structures, or localization requirements will be routed through the formal change management process defined in this SOW. Cross-functional alignment will be maintained across Google, Bristlecone, and approved partner stakeholders through regular governance reviews and dependency tracking.

6.1.content:
Delivery will follow a phased agile model across Prepare, Explore, Realize, and Deploy, executed through three coordinated release waves. Prepare will mobilize the joint team, confirm governance, baseline the project plan and charter, and finalize the execution approach across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, data, integration, testing, and change-management workstreams. Explore will complete blueprinting, fit-gap validation, localization workshops, business-scenario mapping, risk assessment, and design sign-off for the global template and approved local requirements.

Realize will execute baseline configuration, sprint-based build, approved RICEFW development, unit testing, integration data mapping, mock data loads, SIT, regression testing, performance testing, training preparation, and user-readiness activities. Deploy will cover UAT completion, cutover planning, go/no-go governance, production go-live, hypercare, knowledge transfer, and closure.

The rollout will be sequenced by release so that Phase 1 enables TSMC purchase-order capability, Phase 2 establishes the wafer-to-finished-goods MVP, and Phase 3 extends approved additional finished-goods scope and related capabilities. The process-flow and architecture diagrams approved in earlier sections will be used as the governing visual baseline for rollout planning and cross-workstream alignment.

7.1.content:
Project governance will operate through a three-tier structure: executive steering, program management, and workstream delivery. The executive steering layer will provide strategic direction, resolve cross-functional business issues, confirm milestone readiness, and approve decisions with scope, timeline, or commercial impact. The program management layer will manage day-to-day delivery governance, integrated planning, risk and dependency tracking, issue management, and cross-workstream coordination across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, data, testing, and change management. Workstream leads and designated business and IT stakeholders will govern detailed design, sprint execution, integration alignment, test readiness, and release preparation.

Escalation will follow the lowest effective level first. Workstream issues will be raised to the Program Manager for resolution and tracking. Items affecting architecture, cross-system data flow, business process design, milestone dates, localization, or external dependencies will be escalated to the relevant Google business and IT leads and then to the executive steering layer if not resolved within the agreed governance cadence. Any proposed change to approved scope, integrations, timelines, or deliverables will be routed through the formal change management process defined in Section 17.

10.content:
- The global design template, localization requirements, and key design decisions will be baselined and approved before configuration and build proceed for the affected scope.
- Delivery will follow the approved phased agile model across Prepare, Explore, Realize, and Deploy, with three coordinated release waves and milestone governance at each phase transition.
- Google will provide timely participation from business process owners, process leads, IT/BSA stakeholders, and core users for workshops, design reviews, scenario validation, testing, training, and sign-off activities.
- Existing planning, collaboration, and integration patterns across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and approved dependent systems will be retained where feasible and extended through approved delta changes rather than replaced wholesale.
- Integration scope is limited to the approved interfaces and data flows defined in this SOW; any additional interfaces, source systems, target systems, or material scope expansion will require change control.
- Localization is limited to approved requirements for the in-scope Taiwan and North America footprint; any new regional, site, partner, or regulatory requirement identified after design baseline may affect scope, timeline, and commercials.
- Google will make required business, master data, integration, and test data available in line with the project plan to support design validation, build, mock loads, SIT, UAT, cutover, and deployment readiness.
- Google-staffed Controlling support and designated integration, architecture, and business stakeholders will be available as needed for cross-system decisions, validation, and approvals.
- Security roles analysis, data architecture finalization, localization validation, and approved RICEFW scope will be completed in time to support downstream build and testing activities.
- Training, organizational change management, and readiness activities will be executed in alignment with the release plan, including core team train-the-trainer, end-user readiness, cutover support, and go-live support.
- Hypercare covers post-go-live stabilization and knowledge transfer through the agreed transition period only; ongoing run support is outside this SOW unless separately approved.
- Any deviation from these assumptions will be reviewed through the Change Management Process defined in Section 17.

12.1.content:

16.1.content:

17.content:
Changes to approved scope, deliverables, release content, integrations, custom development, timelines, staffing, delivery location, or commercials will be managed only through the formal Change Request process below. No change becomes in scope through workshop discussion, backlog capture, design review, or execution urgency alone.

| Step | Activity | Owner | Timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CR raised | Google or Bristlecone workstream lead identifies the requested change, states the business or technical reason, and submits the request to the Program Manager with enough detail to assess scope, schedule, and cost impact. | Requesting Party / Workstream Lead | Within 2 business days of identifying the change |
| 2 | CR logged | The Program Manager records the CR in the change log, assigns a tracking ID, confirms the affected release, deliverables, and dependencies, and routes it to the relevant owners for assessment. | Bristlecone Program Manager | Within 1 business day of receipt |
| 3 | Impact assessment | The joint team assesses impact on scope, effort, integrations, data, testing, cutover, timeline, resourcing, assumptions, and commercials, and documents whether the change should be approved, deferred, split by release, or rejected. | Bristlecone Program Manager with Google business and IT owners | Within 5 business days of logging, unless the parties agree a longer period for complex changes |
| 4 | CR reviewed / approved | The assessed change is reviewed through the agreed governance forum. Changes with material scope, milestone, release, or commercial impact require written approval from authorized Google and Bristlecone representatives before work begins on the changed scope. | Google Program stakeholders and authorized Bristlecone representatives | At the next scheduled governance review, or earlier if required for a critical path decision |
| 5 | SOW amendment / addendum | If approved, the parties update the applicable project baseline, including scope, deliverables, release plan, acceptance items, staffing, and commercials, and execute any required amendment, addendum, or written approval record. | Google and Bristlecone Program Management with `<LEGAL: confirm required approval form under the governing agreement>` | Before execution of the approved change |
| 6 | CR closure | After approval, rejection, or deferral, the Program Manager updates the CR log, communicates the disposition, and reflects approved changes in the integrated project plan and affected work products. | Bristlecone Program Manager | Within 2 business days of final decision |

Urgent actions needed to protect production readiness, cutover execution, or issue containment may be started only to the minimum extent necessary to stabilize the program. Any resulting scope, timeline, or commercial impact will still be assessed and regularized through this process.
